proof_audit.topic: Identification, local rank, calibration and compact argmax consistency
proof_audit.reasoning: The observable map is defined under maintained restrictions before optimization. The original cost-only family is a global observational-equivalence witness, while known instruments identify the richer experiment under exclusions. For a continuous population criterion on compact Theta with a unique maximizer, the supremum over the closed complement of any open neighborhood has a strictly positive gap. Uniform criterion error less than one third of that gap, together with a sufficiently small optimization error, excludes that complement. This proves consistency without inferring uniform convergence from pointwise convergence. Full-rank local derivatives do not rule out distant observational equivalence; calibration imports a primitive or restriction.
proof_audit.limits: The compact separation argument is proved; applications must establish their own uniform law and unique target. Sample fit and an optimizer certificate do not establish structural identification or policy invariance.

proof_audit.topic: Finite structural supply-demand law, excluded shifts and the tax intervention
proof_audit.reasoning: I independently equated demand and supply in all 16 equally weighted sign states. Orthogonal sign coefficients reproduce each covariance and partialled OLS slope. Z shifts supply and is uncorrelated with U; W shifts demand and is uncorrelated with V. T=Z+U remains relevant but has Cov(T,U)=1. In the distinct noiseless law, substituting P=3+Z/3 into c+dP-gZ gives the whole family c=4-3d, g=(2+d)/3 for every d>0. Applying a producer-price tax to the maintained supply equation produces d-dependent counterfactuals. The observational-equivalence claim is restricted to that cost-only law.

proof_audit.topic: Minimum-distance projection, rank, pseudo-truth and exact Gaussian parameter law
proof_audit.reasoning: Positive weights and the two linearly independent columns of G make G-prime W G positive definite. Completing the square gives the unique unconstrained projection. I derived its coefficients from centered weighted regression and basis perturbations, obtaining the exact 2 by 3 linear map without the author inverse routine. For the explicitly stipulated Gaussian moment experiment, that linear map gives exact normal parameters and covariance V/N. The nonzero residual demonstrates misspecification and weight-dependent pseudo-truth. The price-five ratio is differentiated only locally around a positive slope; exact normality of the numerator and denominator does not make their ratio normal or ensure finite moments.

proof_audit.topic: Perfect-fit extrapolation family and global output optimality
proof_audit.reasoning: The cubic perturbation vanishes at the three observed quantities. Its marginal-cost derivative is 2-kappa+3*kappa*(q-1)^2, at least one on q>=0 for kappa in [0,1]. This establishes strict monotonicity and, after integration, at least quadratic cost growth. Signs at q=3 and q=6 bracket the unique price-13 crossing; profit rises before it and falls after it, so the crossing is the global constrained optimum. Implicit differentiation is valid because the derivative is bounded away from zero. Observed fit leaves kappa and policy output unresolved.

proof_audit.topic: Gaussian simulation stream law and common random numbers
proof_audit.reasoning: I assigned an independent Gaussian coordinate to each actual and simulated draw and collected its coefficient in the estimator. Distinct draw sets by record give 1/N+1/(NR); one R-draw set shared by all records gives 1/N+1/R. In the latter design the realized simulation average remains at fixed R as N increases, so the conditional limit is theta0-Zbar_R. Reusing the same draws at two parameter trials cancels the additive simulation error and gives derivative one; independently redrawing gives 2/(R*h^2). Sharing across parameter trials and sharing across observations are distinct probability contracts.

proof_audit.topic: Finite-atom simulated likelihood: target, uniform law and sandwich
proof_audit.reasoning: For the four atoms (Y,Z), I recomputed expected score, negative curvature and centered score variance directly. All probabilities lie in [1/20,19/20], so each log and its derivatives are bounded on the declared compact parameter interval. Strict concavity and opposite endpoint score signs give the unique interior pseudo-target. Four empirical frequencies provide an actual uniform LLN, not a pointwise shortcut. The interior score expansion, finite-atom iid CLT and convergent Hessian give the stated scalar sandwich. Jensen bias concerns the criterion; it does not force parameter bias at every truth. At the symmetric truth the target derivative is 21/29 rather than one, so the smaller pointwise variance is not an efficiency contradiction for regular estimation of the structural Bernoulli probability.

proof_audit.topic: Growing simulation count consistency and its limited conclusion
proof_audit.reasoning: The log map has Lipschitz constant 20 on the positive probability domain. Each simulator error is one fifth of a mean of R signs, giving a uniform criterion discrepancy bounded by 4 times the average absolute sign mean. Its expected value is at most 4/sqrt(R) by Cauchy-Schwarz. Taking the supremum before expectation and applying Markov establishes uniform closeness as R grows. The ordinary Bernoulli likelihood has a two-frequency uniform LLN. Combining these facts with compact separation proves consistency when the population maximizer belongs to the maintained compact interval.
proof_audit.limits: This argument establishes consistency, not an efficient root-N limit or a universal required simulation rate; it applies to this bounded independent-sign simulator.

proof_audit.topic: Indirect inference, shared covariates, global identification and both boundaries
proof_audit.reasoning: Writing z=theta^2 maps [0,3] bijectively to [0,9]; least squares therefore projects D onto that interval and takes the nonnegative square root. The data and retained-X simulations share a Gaussian coordinate, giving covariance one and difference variance 1+1/H. Fresh simulated X removes that covariance and changes simulation variance. The displayed uniform squared-criterion bound tends to zero under the exact Gaussian D law and gives consistency by compact separation. Interior differentiation gives the 1/(2*theta0) factor. At zero, N^(1/4) scaling produces sqrt(max(Z,0)); at three, the clipped square-root difference gives min(Z/6,0). Both have an atom one half. Global identification on the nonnegative domain includes zero despite zero local rank; signed alternatives violate global identification at nonzero values.

proof_audit.topic: Centered Gumbel expected maximum and softmax from the distribution
proof_audit.reasoning: The right tail is bounded by an exponential and the left tail is double exponential, so the mean and expected maximum absolute shock are finite. Multiplying the independent Gumbel CDFs identifies the maximum as a standard Gumbel plus log-sum-exp. Subtracting the common mean from each shock leaves expected maximum exactly log-sum-exp, without an omitted Euler constant. The choice probability follows by integrating one density against all other CDFs and substituting w=exp(-x). A common shock-location shift adds kappa/(1-beta) to value and cancels from every choice comparison.

proof_audit.topic: Bellman contraction, residual certificate, information and infinite-horizon optimality
proof_audit.reasoning: Monotonicity and translation equivariance make log-sum-exp one-Lipschitz in the sup norm; multiplying continuation by beta gives a contraction for 0<=beta<1. The fixed-point residual bounds value error by delta/(1-beta). I separately read the final information refinement: the predetermined state and both fresh current shocks are observed before action; future shocks are unobserved; action determines the next state. For each admissible nonanticipating policy, bounded deterministic payoffs plus an integrable maximum absolute shock give the uniform tail C*beta^H/(1-beta). Finite-horizon backward induction gives T^H0, and truncation/extension with that tail identifies the infinite-horizon supremum with the contraction limit. A measurable current-shock maximizing stationary rule satisfies the iterated conditional Bellman equality; bounded terminal V and the absolute tail yield attainment. Thus the control interpretation follows from verification, not contraction alone.
proof_audit.limits: These are the two root-origin refinements supplied on promotion, independently checked and resolved. Undiscounted beta=1 is outside the proof.

proof_audit.topic: Dynamic value derivatives, inverse choices and observation law
proof_audit.reasoning: The softmax-weighted transition matrix has stochastic rows, so the Neumann series for (I-beta P)^-1 converges in sup norm. The implicit value derivatives therefore exist under the normalized finite-state model, and choice derivatives include continuation responses. My independent oracle instead substitutes t=exp((V1-V0)/2) at beta=1/2, solves the strictly increasing positive-root cubic on [sqrt(ell),1], and differentiates that polynomial. It reproduces both value and probability derivative columns. Choice ratios identify Delta and c, but r varies with unknown beta while the two baseline choice rates stay fixed. The 36 observations are independent, once-observed agents with fixed initial-state counts; the product likelihood is not a likelihood conditioned on all future states of a single trajectory. Stationary probabilities are a separate repeated-chain calculation. Normalized utility subsidies do not identify dollar welfare.

Changing an approximate value by at most e perturbs every action index by at most beta*e. The chosen index term and log-sum-exp term each change by at most that amount; thus any log choice probability changes by at most 2*beta*e. Combining with the residual certificate and summing 36 independent-record log terms gives the displayed bounds. The peer oracle tests an intentionally inexact value against the separately solved cubic and verifies both actual value and log-probability errors lie below the certificate.
proof_audit.limits: A numerical approximation certificate is not statistical coverage, primitive identification, or evidence that the policy counterfactual is invariant.

proof_audit.topic: Every logit equilibrium, fold tangency and local selection sensitivity
proof_audit.reasoning: A continuous adoption map on [0,1] has a fixed point by the endpoint sign argument. Absolute interaction below four yields a contraction. For b=4*log(3), the log-odds inverse F has exactly two critical points, derivative signs plus/minus/plus and infinite endpoint limits. Reflection gives opposite fold heights; a nonzero second derivative gives tangency. These facts prove three roots strictly between fold heights, two distinct roots at a fold, and one outside. The implicit derivative q(1-q)/(1-b*q(1-q)) is restricted to regular branches. I solved instead in log-odds coordinates with analytic critical cuts and a proved finite root bound, including both folds and the immediately adjacent regions.

proof_audit.topic: Iteration stability, equilibrium outcomes and randomized-selection means
proof_audit.reasoning: At a regular fixed point, the stipulated naive iteration has derivative b*q*(1-q), which is below one on the two baseline outer roots and above one in the middle. This is a property of that computational/dynamic rule, not an observed economic selection theorem. At each policy shift the realized model outcome set remains the finite set of roots. Allowing a probability distribution over those roots produces every mean in their convex hull, which in one dimension is the closed extreme-root interval. Neither that interval nor the root set is a sampling confidence interval.
